ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

2. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

3. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

4. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

5. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

6. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

7. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

9. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the Library

10. When practising Speaking Fluency: pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

11. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

12. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non-Fiction Texts Poems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
